newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm, boosted by stronger Irish pound.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm, boosted by stronger Irish pound.

text.p: Irish bonds firmed, particularly in the shorter paper, in midmorning trade on Friday, boosted by a firmer Irish pound and support from Ireland's Central Bank and National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA), dealers said.

"The front end has seen a good bit of recovery this morning. We have seen good domestic and foreign buying interest in the five-year area, particularly domestic," Padraic Garvey, economist at Riada Stockbrokers, said.

"The Irish market has been helped by the fact that the Irish Central Bank has pushed liquidity into the market. We have also seen NTMA bid support come into the shorts. Plus the Irish pound is up two and a half pfennigs versus the mark and over a penny against sterling," he added.

By 1000 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 50 pence from Thursday's close at 101.75 to yield 6.02 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 rose 30 pence from the close to 108.60 to yield 6.71 percent.
Irish bonds outperformed German bonds by one basis point in the 10-year area and by 10 basis points in the five-year area.
Garvey said the market was surprised on Thursday to see Ireland's Central Bank raise the official short-term facility rate to 6.75 percent from 6.25 percent, effective today.

"It was a bit of a surprise. The market was aware that the one-month money rate was above the short term facility rate but it didn't think we would see March adjusted private sector credit growth of 18.6 percent," Garvey said.
"The Central Bank had every right to raise rates. Indeed, the market would have been surprised today if it hadn't," he added.
Garvey said the market was of the opinion that retail and mortgage rates would rise later on Friday.
Looking ahead, Garvey said market focus was likely to remain on the Irish pound while investors were also awaiting U.S. employment figures.

The payroll total is forecast to rise by 211,000 in April, while average hourly earnings are seen rising by 0.3 percent against 0.4 percent previously. Unemployment is expected to remain unchanged at 5.2 percent.
